source_text: Ut enim hic in potestate diaboli parvulos a Deo reos formari dixisti, ita in inferioribus libri tui partibus taetrius aliquid, quam sunt Manichaeorum sacramenta, vomuisti dicens de Deo: Sic creat malos, quomodo pascit et nutrit malos [n171] .
pass_a_gloss: For as here you have said little ones are formed by God defendants in the power of the devil, so in the inferior parts of your book you have vomited something more foul than are the sacraments of the Manichaeans, saying of God: Thus he creates evils, as he feeds and nourishes evils.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis
LS creo; Blaise of God as maker

pass_b_english: Just as you said here that God forms infants guilty and under the devil’s power, so in later parts of your book you vomited out something more repulsive than the Manichaean mysteries, saying about God: ‘He creates evil people in the same way as he feeds and nourishes evil people.’ [The source compares Isaiah 45:7.]

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
